newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: French troops fight Central Africa mutineers.
newsitem.headline: French troops fight Central Africa mutineers.

text.p: French troops based in the Central African Republic engaged mutinous government troops on Thursday for the first time since a revolt by some army units erupted in the capital Bangui last month, reporters there said.

A correspondent for French radio in Bangui said French troops opened fire as rebels launched another attack. The manager of the Sofitel hotel, which came under mortar fire, said French troops had taken positions in the premises and had asked to use the building's rooftop to get a better view of the rebels.
Mortar bombs fell close to the hotel and many guests fled in the night, the manager said. Earlier a hotel worker said the building, close to the French embassy, had been badly hit.

French troops in the former colony have been protecting the presidential palace and other key sites in the capital but have not intervened in fighting until now. They used helicopter gunships and armoured vehicles to quell a bloodier army uprising in May.
Residents said mutineers based in the Kassai barracks on the eastern outskirst of town used mortars and other heavy weapons for the first time. Rebels control the barracks and the main armoury there.
A two-week-old mutiny, the country's third this year, has shifted from grievances over pay and status to rebel demands for the resignation of elected President Ange-Felix Patasse.
